criteria.criterion: A test in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs runs an easy job (hard_reason null, `[job_plan] mode = "hard"`) whose Behavior criterion says a test 'fails without the fix': planner and critic are called and the verifier prompt contains the 'fails-without-1' record. Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core run::tests`.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: 52 passed, including an_easy_job_whose_behavior_criterion_asks_for_a_fails_without_run_is_planned_in_hard_mode. The test sets mode = "hard" and asserts the reader's hard_reason is null. It checks the roles run in order Reader, Planner, Critic, Producer, Verifier, that there is 1 plan and 1 critique, and that the verifier prompt's '## Checks Athena ran on this tree' section contains 'fails-without-1: not a check' and 'failed without the fix (exit 1)'. With the old gate, plans(false) in hard mode returns false, so these role assertions would fail.

criteria.criterion: A test runs an easy job in `hard` mode with no such criterion and asserts no planner or critic call and no plan record. Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core run::tests` and `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test job_plan`.
criteria.evidence: an_easy_job_in_hard_mode_without_a_fails_without_criterion_is_not_planned passed. It covers three cases: behavior 'the tests still pass', behavior 'the build never fails', and a content criterion 'a test fails without the fix'. Each asserts roles [Reader, Producer, Verifier], (plans, critiques) == (0, 0) and no 'fails-without-' text in the prompt, with empty planner and critic queues. In the CLI run (29 passed), the existing with_athena_toml_planning_hard_jobs_only_... test still passes; its default scenario criterion is 'the tests still pass'.

criteria.criterion: The CLI test in crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs for an easy job with a fails-without criterion checks the plan records and that the verifier prompt contains the fails-without-1 record. Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test job_plan`.
criteria.evidence: an_easy_job_with_a_fails_without_criterion_is_planned_in_hard_mode_and_the_verifier_sees_the_record passed. It uses the repository's own athena.toml [job_plan] (asserted to be mode Hard) and reader_scenario(null). It sets criterion [1], which is the behavior criterion per common/mod.rs:359, to 'A test fails without the fix'. It asserts Landed, the five roles in order, job-plan-1.json and critique-1.json at HEAD, no check_history violations, and 'fails-without-1: not a check' in seen_by_verifier[1].

criteria.criterion: The planning gate in crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs (grep `plans(`) is `hard_reason.is_some() || <helper>(&reading)`, and the helper is a small named function with a doc comment that matches singular and plural wordings (e.g. 'tests fail without the change') of a failing run without the fix in Behavior criterion text. The diff shows the original `plans(reading.hard_reason.is_some())` alone would not plan such a job.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. The gate is now `p.plans(reading.hard_reason.is_some() || asks_for_fails_without_run(&reading))`, and the removed line is `p.plans(reading.hard_reason.is_some())`. asks_for_fails_without_run is a small function with a `///` doc comment. It filters to CriterionKind::Behavior and calls asks_for_failing_run_without_the_fix, which lowercases the text, strips punctuation, and requires a word starting with `fail` plus an anchor phrase. The unit test the_fails_without_helper_matches_singular_and_plural_wordings covers 'Tests fail without the change', 'tests failed without the patch' and 'is failing without the mechanism', and passed in my run of run::tests. JobPlanConfig::plans(false) in hard mode is false, so the old line alone would not plan such a job.

criteria.criterion: docs/design/job-planning.md and CHANGELOG.md state that a job with a 'fails without the fix' criterion is planned even when judged easy.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. job-planning.md adds a paragraph under the hard-mode bullet: 'One more job is planned in `hard` mode even when judged easy: one with a Behavior criterion that asks for a failing run without the fix...'. It also names the root cause and the matching rules. CHANGELOG.md adds an entry under [Unreleased] > Fixed: 'In `hard` planning mode, a job judged easy is now planned when a Behavior criterion asks for a failing run without the fix', with the root cause.

criteria.criterion: Outcome check: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` pass, and the existing mode tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs and crates/athena-data/src/config.rs pass unchanged.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks for this tree: fmt passed, clippy passed, and cargo test --locked passed with 2151 tests. In the diff, config.rs changes only doc comments on PlanMode::Hard and JobPlanConfig::plans, with no test or signature change. job_plan.rs only adds a new test, so the existing mode tests (with_athena_toml_planning_hard_jobs_only_..., a_hard_reading_with_planning_enabled_for_every_job_...) are unchanged and passed in my job_plan run.

findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs changed but is not on the expected deliverables list.
findings.evidence: The diff removes #[cfg(test)] from demo_seam::Guard/install and adds #[derive(Debug)]. This file is outside the brief's six expected deliverables. It is in the critic-accepted planned files, though, and criterion 3's CLI test needs it so that athena-cli tests can install a demo runner. The module stays gated on cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support")), so production builds are unaffected.

findings.summary: Soundness: the gate matches keywords in free text, and some broad anchors can give false positives.
findings.evidence: A 'fail*' word anywhere plus ' without it ' or ' on the base ' anywhere in the text, or any 'fail* without', matches. For example, 'the job fails without a network connection' or 'a failing test on the base is marked pre-existing' would match. A false positive only costs one planning round and does not escalate the producer, and the more correct fix (a structured fails_without field on Criterion) is explicitly out of scope. Better to propose that field as follow-up than to grow the phrase list.

findings.summary: Athena's revert runs for criteria 1 and 3 failed because the tests did not compile, not because an assertion failed.
findings.evidence: With the fix reverted, run::tests fails to compile on the missing asks_for_fails_without_run, and job_plan fails to compile on the missing install_demo_runner. So the revert runs do not show the gate assertions failing on their own. Reading the code shows they would fail: with hard_reason null, the old plans(false) in hard mode yields roles [Reader, Producer, Verifier].

summary: The change passes. In `hard` mode, a job judged easy is now planned when one of its Behavior criteria asks for a failing run without the fix, so the verifier is shown Athena's run of that demonstration. I ran both targeted test suites and they pass: 52 tests in the core run tests and 29 in the CLI job_plan tests. The new core and CLI tests check that the planner and critic are called, that the plan records are kept, and that the verifier's prompt holds the fails-without-1 record. They also check that jobs without such a criterion are not planned. The gate is now `hard_reason.is_some() || asks_for_fails_without_run(&reading)`, with a documented helper. The design doc and changelog both state the new behavior and its root cause. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs passed, and the existing mode tests are unchanged. There are three minor findings. First, checks.rs changed outside the expected deliverables list; it was planned and is needed for the CLI test. Second, the free-text matching can catch some unrelated wordings; a wrong match only costs one planning round, and the structured field that would fix this is out of scope. Third, Athena's runs with the fix reverted failed because the tests did not compile, not on the gate assertions themselves; reading the code shows those assertions would fail too.
